issue: Carve-out path resolves the same StamphogRepoConfig twice (or thrice) per delivery

verdicts.evidence: pr72680_tree/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:179 (_resolve_repo_config inside _inbox_rereview_carve_out), :876-880 (carve-out call, provenance kept), :918 (unconditional re-resolve on main path — duplication confirmed), :298-304 (single indexed filter/first query), :858 and :891 (module already re-resolves per retry-guarded block by design)
verdicts.notes: Premise is factually accurate: a carved-out delivery resolves StamphogRepoConfig twice (line 179 in the carve-out, line 918 on the main path). But it is one extra single-row indexed query in a Celery task on a rare path (bot-authored self-driving inbox re-reviews), with no correctness/security/contract dimension. The module intentionally re-resolves the config in each independently retry-guarded block (lines 858, 891, 918), so the "duplication" matches the file's deliberate freshness+retry pattern; threading the config through the frozen _InboxCarveOut would add coupling for negligible gain. Micro-optimization, not a real issue.

verdicts.evidence: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:179 (`repo_config = _resolve_repo_config(installation_id, repo)` inside `_inbox_rereview_carve_out`) and tasks.py:918 (identical call in `process_pull_request_event` main path). For a qualifying inbox re-review, `skip_reason` is always set (self-driving PRs are bot-authored drafts, per comment at ~line 869), so the carve-out runs and resolves the config; when it returns a non-None provenance the function proceeds to line 918 and re-runs the exact same writer-pinned query. A base retarget adds a third call at line 858. `_resolve_repo_config` (def at ~line 289 region) is a single `.filter(provider, installation_id, repository).order_by("created_at","id").first()` point lookup on the small StamphogRepoConfig table.
verdicts.notes: The redundant read exists exactly as described, so it is not speculative. But impact is negligible: one extra indexed point-lookup on a tiny table, on a cold path (only bot-authored self-driving inbox PRs receiving synchronize/reopen/retarget webhooks), not N+1 or hot-loop. The handler deliberately re-resolves config in each branch inside its own retry-wrapped try/except (lines 858, 891, 918), so threading the carve-out's config through would couple the helper's return to the main path for a sub-millisecond saving. Valid low-stakes observation; the original should_fix severity overstates it — consider is right.

this_experiment_findings.title: Carve-out path resolves the repo config twice on the writer database
this_experiment_findings.problem: When the carve-out positively identifies a self-driving PR, _inbox_rereview_carve_out resolves the repo config at line 179 (writer-pinned, unscoped). Control then flows past the skip block, and process_pull_request_event resolves the same config again at line 918 before creating the run. Every inbox re-review pays two writer-database round trips for one row. The two reads can also disagree in a race (a config disabled between them), which the later enabled check happens to absorb, but the duplicate work is pure overhead on the webhook hot path.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Return the resolved config inside _InboxCarveOut and reuse it at line 918 when inbox_review is not None, falling back to a fresh _resolve_repo_config only for the normal path. Keep the enabled re-check on the reused row.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim and anchor (tasks.py:179 and ~918): the carve-out resolves StamphogRepoConfig and process_pull_request_event resolves it again per delivery.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Premise traced and confirmed: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` calls `_resolve_repo_config` at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:179, and when it returns provenance (line 208-215) the caller `process_pull_request_event` (tasks.py:876 -> inbox_review set at 879) falls through the skip block and calls `_resolve_repo_config` again at tasks.py:918. `_resolve_repo_config` (tasks.py:289-304) is one `.filter(provider, installation_id, repository).order_by().first()` single-row query pinned to the writer. So two reads do happen on that branch.

Refutation facts: (1) The path is not the webhook HTTP hot path. `process_pull_request_event` is a `@shared_task` Celery task (tasks.py:809-810); the comments at 871-872 and 913-915 state the webhook was already ACKed before this code runs. (2) The branch is reachable only for bot-authored (tasks.py:168), repo-native-branch (174-177), synchronize/reopen/retarget (166) deliveries that also match a signal-implementation task run via the tasks facade (189-196) and a resolver callback (201-205) — a rare branch whose cost is dominated by those calls and the run creation that follows. (3) Independent re-resolution is the established pattern in this module, not an accident of this change: line 858 (`retarget_config`) and line 891 (`skip_repo_config`) each resolve the config separately from line 918 as well. (4) The second read is load-bearing: tasks.py:925-939 re-checks `enabled` on a fresh snapshot and retracts standing approvals on a head-changing action if the repo was disabled; the suggestion to reuse the carve-out's row "with the enabled re-check" cannot re-check without another read, so the refactor either keeps the query or widens the disable window.
fresh_votes.refutation: The duplicate query is factually present but is one index-backed single-row read on a rare, already-async Celery branch (not the webhook request path), sits next to two other independent config resolutions the module already does by design (tasks.py:858, 891), and the second read gives the `enabled` gate at tasks.py:925 a fresh snapshot that the proposed reuse would discard. No user-visible consequence, no N+1, no unbounded growth: this is a micro-optimization preference, not a defect.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Worktree: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215, file products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py.

The factual premise holds: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` calls `_resolve_repo_config` at tasks.py:179, and when it returns provenance, `process_pull_request_event` calls `_resolve_repo_config` again at tasks.py:918. `_resolve_repo_config` (tasks.py:289-304) is a single-row `.filter(provider, installation_id, repository).order_by(...).first()` pinned to the writer via `router.db_for_write`.

But the duplicate is neither new nor accidental. The same function already re-resolves the config per delivery on two other legs of this exact code path, each inside its own retry envelope: the base-retarget block at tasks.py:858 resolves, then tasks.py:918 resolves again on the same delivery; the untrusted-skip block at tasks.py:891 resolves independently too. Per-delivery re-resolution is the established design of this function, with the docstring at tasks.py:294-296 explaining the writer pin is there so a config "synced or toggled moments before the webhook" is not missed, i.e. freshness is the point.

The second read at tasks.py:918 feeds the `enabled` check at tasks.py:925, and when disabled and `action in _HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` it calls `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` (tasks.py:929). The finding admits the race is "absorbed" by this check; the suggested fix (reuse the row from line 179) would make line 925 test a snapshot taken before `find_signal_implementation_run` (tasks.py:189-196) and the resolver callback (tasks.py:201-205), so a repo disabled in that window would be re-reviewed with no approval retraction. "Keep the enabled re-check on the reused row" cannot re-check without the very query it removes.

Reachability: `_is_bot_authored` at tasks.py:171 returns early for every human PR before any DB read; only bot-authored, repo-native (tasks.py:176-178), head-changing deliveries that also match a task-facade signal run AND whose acting reviewer opted in reach both reads. Non-inbox bots (dependabot/renovate) pay the line-179 read but return at tasks.py:198 and never reach line 918. On the deliveries that do reach both, the extra indexed single-row query sits beside a facade run lookup, a resolver callback, a full `ReviewRun` creation transaction and the GitHub API traffic downstream.

Tests: products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py has no `assertNumQueries`/`CaptureQueriesContext` anywhere; the carve-out tests (test_tasks.py:762, 796, 850, 875) assert behavior only (queued run, provenance dict, single facade call). No test guards the query count, and no test would change under either shape.
fresh_votes.refutation: The claim is a true statement about two indexed single-row reads, not a defect. The code already resolves the repo config more than once per delivery by design (tasks.py:858 then 918; tasks.py:891 on the skip leg), each read bounded by its own retry, because the writer-pinned resolver exists to see a config toggled moments earlier. Removing the second read would trade that freshness away: the `enabled` check at tasks.py:925 and its approval retraction at 929 would run on a snapshot taken before the facade lookup and resolver callback, widening the window in which a just-disabled repo still gets a re-review. The path is reachable only for opted-in, task-linked, bot-authored PR pushes, where one extra `.first()` query is negligible next to the run-creation transaction. No user-visible consequence, no N+1, no unbounded growth, no test exposure: this is a micro-optimization preference with a real downside, so is_real=false.

fresh_votes.evidence: Premise is factually true and the trigger is reachable in production: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` calls `_resolve_repo_config` at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:179, and when it returns a provenance the caller falls through the skip block (tasks.py:884-914) and calls `_resolve_repo_config` again at tasks.py:918. `_resolve_repo_config` (tasks.py:289-304) is one single-row `.filter(provider, installation_id, repository).order_by(...).first()` pinned to `router.db_for_write`. The path is live in prod config: review_hog registers the resolver at import (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:69 `register_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver(resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer)`), the `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle exists (receivers.py:154, migration 0019), and the carve-out is only entered for bot-authored, repo-native, head-changing deliveries (tasks.py:167-176). On a base retarget the same delivery already does a third read at tasks.py:858 by design. No query-count test exists in products/stamphog/backend/tasks/ (grep for assertNumQueries/CaptureQueriesContext returned nothing), so nothing pins the count either way.
fresh_votes.refutation: The extra query is not a defect. (1) Cost: one indexed single-row read on a branch that only fires for opted-in self-driving PR pushes, and that same delivery already performs the tasks-facade run lookup (tasks.py:189-196), a review_hog resolver callback (tasks.py:201-205), and a run creation, so the second read is noise; "webhook hot path" is not accurate for this branch since every human PR exits at tasks.py:168-171 before any DB touch. (2) The second read is load-bearing, not redundant: tasks.py:918-934 takes a fresh snapshot and, if `enabled` flipped between the two reads, retracts standing approvals on head-changing actions (tasks.py:925-932). The suggestion "reuse the row and keep the enabled re-check" is self-contradicting: a re-check on a cached row cannot observe a change without another read, so the refactor either re-introduces the query or widens the window in which a just-disabled repo still re-reviews. The finding itself concedes the race "the later enabled check happens to absorb". A duplicated read that serves as a freshness safeguard, with no user-visible consequence, is a style/micro-optimization preference, not a real finding.
